title: 3 Magnets, 4 Pixels Apart… Which One Catches It? 🧲
description:
Gold, aqua or rose: which magnet catches the pendulum? Comment your pick before the bob lets go!

Top view: a steel bob hangs on a string above three magnets at the corners of a triangle: gold (triangle), aqua (circle) and rose (square). It is released from rest at the marked release point. Three things act on it: the string pulls it back toward the center like a spring, each magnet pulls harder the closer the bob gets (inverse-square, softened by the height the bob hangs at), and friction drains its energy, shown on the energy bar. Once the energy drops under the marked line the bob can no longer get away from the magnet it is circling, so that is where it stops, and where it stops wins. Then a second bob is released 4 pixels to the left under the same rules at 3x speed. Finally every one of the 129,600 start points on a 270 by 480 grid is run and colored by the magnet that catches it, and the camera zooms in on the release point.
This is a numerical model, not a lab measurement: fixed-step RK4, the same integrator and step for the bob you watch and for every pixel of the map. A different step or method can move the fine detail. Motion, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 126), with no footage, samples or stock media.
Which magnet did you pick?
#simulation #satisfying #chaos
